Subject: Dedicated pool oversubscription — NovaDev text-gen-prod impact

Hi Aisha,

I wanted to reach out immediately to acknowledge the service disruption your team hit this morning on text-gen-prod. Our telemetry shows a dedicated GPU pool oversubscription event that caused elevated 5xx responses and tail latency between ~08:42 and 09:01 UTC. We pushed an emergency mitigation at 08:58 UTC to route a portion of your traffic to a warm standby region and to temporarily increase burst capacity for your reserved pool.

Quick asks so we can include the right details in the post-incident writeup: can you confirm the exact endpoint(s) you saw errors on (you mentioned text-gen-prod), and paste two or three sample request IDs and timestamps? That will help us correlate traces and reconstruct a precise timeline.

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Ops is running a deeper root-cause investigation and will aim to provide a draft postmortem within 24 hours.
- We'll provide a remediation timeline and, if appropriate, a credit proposal.
- I'll schedule a 30-minute review with your SRE/product lead for tomorrow.

I'm very sorry for the impact — we'll treat this with high priority.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Camila — quick summary from infra (shortform):
- Root cause (preliminary): an allocator metric drift in our autoscaler combined with an upstream preemptible reclaim event in the regional pool. The autoscaler underestimated effective load after a reclaim, allowing new reservations to oversubscribe live nodes.
- Knock-on effect: mass KV-cache invalidations and concurrent warmup (thundering herd) when nodes resumed, producing high tail latency and transient 503s.
- Mitigation performed: rolled an emergency allocator patch at 08:58 UTC to tighten reservation accounting and rate-limit warmup. Also blurred routing to warm standby region for NovaDev traffic.
- Fix status: allocator patch deployed (allocator-fix.diff). Monitoring indicates normalizing metrics by 09:05 UTC and steady p50/p99 thereafter.
- Next steps for durable remediation: backfill autoscaler telemetry to prevent drift, add reclaim-aware headroom heuristics, and a graceful KV-cache priming circuit breaker. We will prepare a formal postmortem and proposed timeline.

I attached the postmortem draft and the small diff we shipped. Happy to jump on a call to walk through the patch.

Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Post-incident update and proposed remediation for NovaDev — INF-8421

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the early data — that helped us converge quickly. Attached is our postmortem PDF (redwood_postmortem_20270625.pdf) and a link to the public Jira ticket tracking the durable fixes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8421. Summary highlights:

- Timeline: Oversubscription observed 08:42–09:01 UTC; emergency fixes deployed 08:58 UTC; full normalization by 09:05 UTC.
- Root cause: autoscaler allocation metric drift + regional preemptible reclaim -> oversubscription -> KV-cache invalidation -> warmup thundering herd.
- Remediations (short/medium term):
  * Short: tightened allocation accounting (deployed), standby routing for critical customers when reclaim signals detected (enabled), and an immediate increase to reserved headroom policy for NovaDev for 48 hours.
  * Medium: reclaim-aware headroom heuristic, telemetry backfills, and a KV priming circuit breaker (tracked INF-8421).
- Customer impact and remedy: we observed ~12% 503s on POST /v1/generate for text-gen-prod. As a gesture while we complete the full RCA, Redwood will apply a 10% service credit for NovaDev's June billing period and extend dedicated pool headroom for 48 hours. I'll confirm credit in writing once billing runs.

We'd like to schedule a 30-minute technical review this week (Ben and Dylan will join) to walk through the postmortem and the planned timeline for INF-8421. Are you available Thursday 10:00–10:30 PT or Friday 14:00–14:30 PT?

Link to postmortem (internal): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Cpostmortem-novadev
Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8421

Best regards,
Camila Reyes
